[OriginalPoster]: Hi everyone, and thanks in advance for any advice. I'm dealing with an ongoing situation at work and I'm not sure how to handle it anymore.

I have a colleague who keeps messaging me about work late at night and on weekends. It's not emergencies, just follow-up questions or ideas that could easily wait until the next workday. I've tried not responding until the morning, and I did once say something like, "I usually disconnect after 6 pm, so I'll get back to you tomorrow." They said they understood, but the late-night messages started up again after a week or so.

It's starting to really stress me out because my phone keeps lighting up and I feel guilty ignoring them, but I also don't want to be available 24/7. I worry that if I push back too hard I'll look uncooperative or damage the working relationship, especially since they're generally nice otherwise.

What are some good ways to set firmer boundaries here without sounding rude or making things awkward? For context, I work in a fairly professional but not super formal office, and we mostly communicate through chat and email. I'm feeling a bit worn out by this and would appreciate some concrete wording suggestions.
rounds.reasoning_summary:
**My Thought Process: Crafting a Helpful Response**

Okay, so the user needs advice on setting boundaries with a colleague who messages late. They've tried before, but it didn't stick, and they want to maintain a good relationship. My goal here is to give practical advice and helpful wording, all while staying polite and concise. I'll focus on action, not just commiseration.

First, I'll acknowledge the stress and validate their need for boundaries. Then, I'll suggest a simple technical solution: using "Do Not Disturb" or muting notifications after hours – a visual cue to disconnect. The key will be the phrasing of the conversation the user needs to have, so I'll create a concrete example. I want the wording to be clear, polite, and frame the boundary as ensuring the colleague's ideas get proper attention during work hours.

I'm aiming for exactly five sentences, so I'll draft the response, then review it against my constraints. I'll make sure it's accurate, courteous, and actionable. After that, I'll go back and edit the sentences so they read a bit better, and have a stronger impact. That's it!
rounds.response: Hello! It is completely understandable to feel stressed, as protecting your downtime is essential for maintaining a healthy work-life balance. First, I highly recommend using the "Do Not Disturb" feature or muting work apps on your phone after 6 pm so you aren't visually prompted to check them. Next, try offering a friendly but firm reminder during regular hours: "Hi [Name], I know you like catching up in the evenings, but I keep my work notifications off after 6 pm; if you have non-urgent ideas then, please use the 'schedule send' feature or email me so I can give them my full attention tomorrow." This frames your boundary around making sure their thoughts don't get lost in the shuffle, which helps prevent any awkwardness. Finally, continue to hold this line by strictly waiting until your workday begins to reply, and they will eventually adapt to your schedule.
